hints: In pre-order, the whole left subtree comes before the right subtree. Which node of the left subtree is visited last? The old right subtree should hang below that node.

Walk down the right pointers with a cur pointer. When cur has a left child, find the rightmost node of that left subtree, attach cur.right there, then move the left subtree over to the right. This needs no extra memory.

1. Set cur = root.
  2. While cur is not null: if cur.left exists, find its rightmost node p.
  3. Set p.right = cur.right, cur.right = cur.left, cur.left = null.
  4. Move cur = cur.right.

approaches.name: Brute force (list)
approaches.idea: Save the nodes in pre-order in a list, then relink them one by one: left = null and right = the next node.

approaches.name: Optimal (rewire in place)
approaches.idea: For each node with a left subtree, attach the old right subtree under the rightmost node of the left subtree, then move the left subtree to the right. Each edge is walked a constant number of times.

explain: Take [3,8,2,6,5,null,1]. At 3, the rightmost node of the left subtree (8, 6, 5) is 5. We attach 2's subtree under 5, move 8 to the right of 3, and clear the left. Now cur moves to 8. Its left is 6, which has no right child, so 5 is attached under 6 and 6 moves to the right of 8. The rest of the chain has no left children, which gives 3→8→6→5→2→1. The pre-order order never changes because each right subtree is attached exactly after the last pre-order node of its left sibling. An empty tree is left as it is.
recognize: When you must restructure a tree in place into pre-order, think of linking each right subtree to the rightmost node of the left subtree, the same trick used in Morris traversal.
